editorial_reason: Checked Stacks Commutative Algebra 10.41, Definition 10.41.1. Going up and going down express different lifting requirements on ordered pairs of prime ideals under a ring map.

definitions.text: A ring map R→S satisfies going up if, given p⊆p′ in Spec(R) and q∈Spec(S) above p, some prime q′⊇q of S lies above p′.
A ring map R→S satisfies going down if, given p⊆p′ in Spec(R) and q′ of S lying above p′, a prime q⊆q′ exists that lies over p.

editorial_reason: Checked Stacks Categories 4.36, Example 4.36.1 and Definition 4.36.2. The Grothendieck construction of a category-valued presheaf yields a fibred category, while a split fibration is isomorphic over the base to such a construction.

definitions.text: A category-valued presheaf on C is a contravariant functor C^op→Cat, assigning a category to each object and compatible pullback functors to arrows in the base.
A fibred category p:E→C is split if it is isomorphic over C to the Grothendieck construction of a strictly contravariant category-valued functor on C.

editorial_reason: Checked Stacks Algebra 10.50, Definition 10.50.1 and Lemmas 10.50.4–10.50.5. Valuation rings have an equivalent fraction-field divisibility criterion, and domination is a separate relation between local rings.

definitions.text: An integral domain V with fraction field K is a valuation ring if each nonzero x∈K has at least one of x and x^{-1} lying in V.
For local subrings A⊆B of a common field, B dominates A if the maximal ideal of B contracts to the maximal ideal of A.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: domination of local rings

definitions.text: A valuation ring is a discrete valuation ring in the Stacks convention if its associated ordered value group is isomorphic to Z, with its usual order.

editorial_reason: Checked Stacks Algebra 10.45, Definition 10.45.1, Lemma 10.45.2 and Definition 10.45.5. It separates a perfect field from its perfect closure, with a Frobenius-based criterion in prime characteristic.

definitions.text: A field k is perfect if every algebraic field extension of k is separable over k; equivalently k has characteristic zero or, in characteristic p>0, every element of k is a pth power.
The perfect closure of a field k of positive characteristic p is its smallest perfect extension obtained by adjoining all compatible p-power roots of elements of k inside a fixed algebraic closure.
definitions.context_hint: Field theory: perfect closure of a field

editorial_reason: Checked Stacks Set Theory 3.4, which explicitly defines ordinals via transitive sets well ordered by membership, and distinguishes successor and limit ordinals.

definitions.text: An ordinal is a transitive set α on which the membership relation ∈ is a well-order: each nonempty subset has an ∈-least element, and every member of α is itself a subset of α.
The successor of an ordinal α is the ordinal α+1=α∪{α}; an ordinal is a successor ordinal if it has this form for some α.
An ordinal λ is a limit ordinal if it is nonzero and is not the successor of any other ordinal.

Checked Stacks 10.56 introductory definitions of graded rings and modules, their irrelevant ideal and degree shifts. These constructions use direct-sum decompositions and compatibility of multiplication or scalar action with degree.

definitions.text: A nonnegatively graded ring S is a direct sum S=⊕_{n≥0}S_n of additive groups satisfying S_nS_m⊆S_{n+m} for every n,m≥0.
definitions.context_hint: Graded commutative algebra: nonnegative ring grading

definitions.text: A graded module M over S=⊕_{n≥0}S_n is an S-module with a direct-sum decomposition M=⊕_{j∈Z}M_j and S_nM_j⊆M_{n+j}.
The degree shift M(n) of a graded module M is the graded module whose degree-j component is M(n)_j=M_{n+j}, preserving the ungraded module structure.
definitions.context_hint: Graded commutative algebra: shift of graded module
